If you started sobriety on the new year, you might be starting to feel good. On the first day of full sobriety, you may of course be recoverying from the effects of the night before. On the second day you'll feel mostly normal, a bit wonky but definitely better than the day before. On the third day, you may start feeling good as your body heals itself. This will continue for a while as your body heals more and more. In a couple days, you may feel more rested than you've been in a long time.

If you are tapering, you've got it within you to bring your daily consumption down to zero. For a conservative taper, if you've been drinking every night for a long time and had 6 beers last night, that means to have 4 tonight, then 2 tomorrow, then you are done. Before you start, state out loud "I will have exactly N drinks tonight" according to your taper schedule. If have N drinks you are JUST ITCHING to have more, find something else pleasant to do, and drink a lot of water of course. I recommend hopping into a warm shower. It'll help your body detox a little and feel good. Stay in there as long as you need. The craving will pass and sobering up will begin to feel better. A few gallons of spent water is nothing compared to the profound benefit of getting your booze under control.

Hope your challenges are going well.
